description: Transition from the imperative command at the end of Al-Wāqi'ah ('So exalt the name of your Lord, the Supreme') to Al-Ḥadīd opening by declaring that all creation across heavens and earth has already fulfilled that glorification.

Transition from Al-Ḥadīd establishing Allah's encompassing knowledge and supreme grace to Al-Mujādilah demonstrating that infinite knowledge in the intimate grievance of a distressed woman heard from above seven heavens.

Transition from Al-Mujādilah defining the Party of Allah and their disavowal of those who oppose Allah and His Messenger to Al-Ḥashr demonstrating the historical expulsion of Banū al-Naḍīr for opposing Allah and His Messenger.

Transition from Al-Ḥashr concluding with the grand litany of Divine Names and cosmic glorification to Al-Mumtaḥanah forbidding the granting of secret love and allegiance to enemies of this Supreme Sovereign.

Transition from Al-Mumtaḥanah forbidding alliance with those under divine wrath to Aṣ-Ṣaff demanding complete integrity between speech and deed, commanding believers to stand as a lead-cemented wall in battle.

Transition from Aṣ-Ṣaff concluding with the disciples supporting Jesus and the prophecy of Ahmad to Al-Jumu'ah initiating continuous praise (Yusabbiḥu) and celebrating the mission of the Messenger sent to the unlettered nation.

Transition from Al-Jumu'ah admonishing the believers for commercial distraction during the sermon to Al-Munāfiqūn exposing the lethal internal threat: the hypocrites using false oaths to camouflage subversion.

Transition from Al-Munāfiqūn closing with the deathbed plea of the hoarder for charity to At-Taghābun revealing the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain where worldly investments are judged in their eternal reality.

Transition from At-Taghābun warning that family trials can become trials of enmity to Aṭ-Ṭalāq providing sacred legal boundaries for marital dissolution with dignity, recurring promises of ease, and uncalculated provision.

Transition from Aṭ-Ṭalāq closing with Allah's knowledge encompassing all things in seven heavens and earth to At-Taḥrīm showing that all-encompassing knowledge penetrating domestic chambers to inform the Prophet of a whispered confidence.

The macro-architectural progression of the Musabbiḥāt: shifting from past tense (Sabbaḥa in 57, 59, 61) to present continuous (Yusabbiḥu in 62, 64), harmonizing celestial hymns with the concrete legal and moral order of Medinan society.
